title: The normalized constant-coset map to lattice classes
statement: For an exact lattice-class sheaf presentation (F,c) [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-pair-image-classification] over a topological field K and subring A, and a rational frame e:L|U ≅ K_U^n, constructed constant-matrix pairs give a natural map from the constant presheaf ULift(GL_n(K)/GL_n(A)) to F|U. It is locally injective. If it is locally surjective, its sheafification is an isomorphism from the constant sheaf to F|U, with the exact embedded-image normalization.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), pp. 59–60; The normalized constant-coset map to lattice classes

proof.text: Choose each matrix pair from the proved existence theorem. Its image formula, image classification and coset invariance make its class independent of the right-coset representative. Define restriction using F.map; image formulas and the restriction clause of the presentation prove normalization on every slice object.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), pp. 59–60; The normalized constant-coset map to lattice classes

proof.text: On a nonempty object, equality of the two classes gives equality of the matrix images on every further object. Evaluate at a point to recover equality of cosets. The equalizer sieve is therefore maximal there; on an empty object it is covering by the empty-cover axiom. Thus the presheaf map is locally injective.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), pp. 59–60; The normalized constant-coset map to lattice classes

proof.text: Extend the map by sheafifyLift. At the required large value universe, the unit of sheafification is locally bijective. The unit factorization transfers local bijectivity to the map of sheaves, hence it is an isomorphism by Mathlib Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso. The unit equation supplies the normalization.
